title: Global monetary tightening and its spillover effects on developing countries
notes: Build-time ETL snapshots are used to avoid browser API calls and improve reproducibility.
Charts are educational and descriptive; they are not forecasting tools.
Local raw artifacts from BIS/World Bank/IMF are ingested when available in data/raw.

evidence.title: Tightening synchronization wave
evidence.body: The TSI panel tracks the share of tracked central banks that are hiking versus cutting each quarter.

evidence.title: Offshore liquidity as transmission channel
evidence.body: GLI series track international credit in major currencies to non-residents, a direct spillover channel.

evidence.title: Debt stress and USD debt exposure
evidence.body: Debt service burden and USD debt composition jointly capture structural refinancing vulnerability.

evidence.title: COFER methodology break
evidence.body: Reserve-share trend line includes a flagged break at 2025-Q3 for publication revision awareness.

breaks.note: COFER publication revision removed unallocated reserves from published tables.

caveats: Country coverage is constrained to economies with complete series in the selected period.
CBPOL meeting-frequency data are quarter-normalized using observed quarter-end values.
WB USD composition series uses IDS source API with counterpart-area WLD.
The simulator is a vulnerability lens, not a predictive model.

executive_summary: The latest quarter (2026-Q1) shows 0% of tracked central banks hiking and 5.9% cutting.
Average developing-country stress score is 45.1, with 11 economies above that benchmark in the latest year.
USD offshore liquidity remains above peer currencies by -3.5 index points, reinforcing dollar funding spillovers.
The top observed stress exposures are Colombia, Argentina, Pakistan, while COFER USD allocated reserve share is 57.2%.

section_notes.title: Pulse interpretation
insights: Latest median policy-rate move: 0 pp; dispersion: 0 pp.

section_notes.title: Synchronization interpretation
insights: Latest quarter hiking share change versus prior quarter: -2.8 percentage points.
Synchronous shifts indicate shared reaction to global inflation and financing conditions.

section_notes.title: Transmission interpretation
insights: USD liquidity index exceeds EUR/JPY mean by -3.5 points in the latest observation.
This supports a funding-channel narrative where dollar conditions tighten broader external financing.

section_notes.title: Country stress interpretation
insights: Coverage includes 19 developing economies with annual debt-service and currency-composition profiles.
Cross-country means: debt service 22% of exports; USD debt share 79.7%.

section_notes.title: Network-core interpretation
insights: A concentrated currency core can transmit tightening rapidly through multi-hop funding relationships.
Periphery currencies are connected through core hubs, not only bilateral channels.

section_notes.title: Methodology interpretation
insights: All chart inputs are generated at build-time and captured in dataset lineage with hashes.
A 2025-Q3 COFER break is explicitly flagged to prevent false trend inferences across methodology changes.
